key_insight: Fine-tuned MACE potentials predict that MgSiO3 post-perovskite conducts lattice heat 44–55% better than bridgmanite at matched lower-mantle conditions.
engineering_relevance: The resulting conductivity parameterizations support lower-mantle thermal models, with core–mantle boundary aggregate estimates consistent with the commonly assumed 10 W/(m K).
method: Fine-tune phase-specific MACE potentials for MgO, bridgmanite, and post-perovskite.
Replace DFT force evaluations in linearized phonon Boltzmann transport calculations.
Combine a quasi-harmonic phase boundary with a model geotherm and aggregate conductivity bounds.
evidence_signal: For MgO at 0 GPa, substituting DFT forces for MACE forces changed calculated conductivity by only 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K.
watch_item: The 9.5–11.4 W/(m K) core–mantle boundary estimate describes an Fe-free aggregate of 80 vol% silicate and 20 vol% MgO, not the full compositional complexity of Earth's mantle.
paper_title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
